PAFAH1B1.mechanism: LIS1/PAFAH1B1, a DISC1-interacting protein important for neuronal migration, shows reduced protein expression in schizophrenia postmortem brain, with expression associated with high-risk DISC1 polymorphisms, implicating the DISC1-LIS1 neurodevelopmental pathway in schizophrenia.

PCDH7.mechanism: PCDH7 SNPs show genome-wide-significant association with antipsychotic treatment response in schizophrenia and colocalize with schizophrenia GWAS risk signal, identifying PCDH7 as a schizophrenia-associated common-variant locus linked to synaptic/neurotransmitter pathways.

PPM1E.mechanism: Promoter histone H3K9K14 acetylation at PPM1E is significantly reduced (hypoacetylated) in prefrontal cortex of young schizophrenia patients versus age-matched controls, linking epigenetic chromatin regulation at this gene to schizophrenia pathophysiology.

RIMS2.mechanism: RIMS2, a cytomatrix active-zone protein regulating synaptic vesicle release, shows increased protein expression in the amygdala of schizophrenia patients, independent of antipsychotic treatment, implicating dysregulated vesicle-release machinery in schizophrenia neurobiology.

ROCK2.mechanism: ROCK2 hyperactivation drives dendritic spine loss and synaptic ultrastructural defects in schizophrenia models; a selective ROCK2 inhibitor rescues prefrontal spine density and produces antipsychotic-like effects in genetic and pharmacological schizophrenia mouse models.

SBNO1.mechanism: SBNO1 is expressed in the developing cortical plate and required for neurite/axon-dendrite outgrowth in cortical neurons; human genetic studies implicate SBNO1 mutations and cortical-morphology-linked genetic-epigenetic interactions as schizophrenia risk factors.

UBE2K.mechanism: UBE2K shows elevated blood and brain protein/mRNA levels correlating with positive psychotic symptom severity in schizophrenia, and is targeted by a circRNA-miRNA-mRNA (ceRNA) post-transcriptional regulatory axis implicated in schizophrenia pathophysiology.
